content: 1. Tazemetostat reduces the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Tecovirimat reduces the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Tecovirimat is a weak inducer of CYP3A4 and decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 4. When coadministering tecovirimat, monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 7. After discontinuing cobicistat, allow a one-week washout period before increasing the temsirolimus dose to its original level. 8. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 10. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 11. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust tezacaftor dosage regimen if coadministered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of theophylline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of theophylline by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of thioridazine through other mechanisms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be necessary upon coadministration. 16. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of timolol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both darunavir and tipranavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE systemic exposure and the risk of adverse effects. 23. Darunavir increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE systemic exposure and the risk of adverse effects. 24. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 25. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 26. Darunavir increases the levels of toremifene by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. The metabolism of toremifene may be inhibited by drugs known to inhibit CYP3A4 hepatic enzymes. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tramadol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. A reduced dose of tramadol may be required. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tramadol by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. A reduced dose of tramadol may be required. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tramadol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. A reduced dose of tramadol may be required. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trazodone through other mechanisms. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Trazodone is a substrate of CYP3A4 and CYP2D6; cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. 31. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of trazodone by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect (e.g., using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose). Monitor for antidepressant response. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant to the desired effect, including using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 35. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trimipramine through other mechanisms. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to the desired effect, including using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor its response during coadministration with TCAs and cobicistat. 37. Ublituximab decreases the effects of darunavir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate; coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 41. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Caution is advised if upadacitinib is coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 43. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 44. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 45. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day; do not exceed 200 mg/day if weight >50 kg. 47. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 48. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 50. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of verapamil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 51. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 52. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of verapamil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 53. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are both CYP3A4 substrates; coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 54. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects that may be associated with increased systemic exposure to vinblastine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. 55. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects that may be associated with increased systemic exposure to vinblastine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. If the antiretroviral regimen must be withheld for a prolonged period, consider initiating a revised regimen that does not include a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor. 56. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vincristine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects that may be associated with increased systemic exposure to vincristine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. 57. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vincristine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects that may be associated with increased systemic exposure to vincristine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. If the antiretroviral regimen must be withheld for a prolonged period, consider initiating a revised regimen that does not include a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor. 58. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 59. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with voriconazole is not recommended unless the benefit/risk assessment justifies its use. 60. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration of cobicistat with voriconazole is not recommended unless the benefit/risk assessment justifies its use. 61. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vortioxetine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 62. Darunavir and warfarin interact through other mechanisms. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Warfarin serum concentrations may be increased or decreased. 63. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of warfarin through other mechanisms. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Warfarin's less potent R-enantiomer is metabolized in part by CYP3A4 (and also CYP1A2 and CYP2C19). Monitor INR more frequently if coadministered with inhibitors of these isoenzymes and adjust warfarin dose if needed. 64. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 65. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zanubrutinib (a CYP3A4 substrate) to 80 mg once daily if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. 66. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zanubrutinib (a CYP3A4 substrate) to 80 mg once daily if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. 67. Darunavir increases the levels of zileuton by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. There is potential for increased toxicity. 68. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 69. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zuranolone dose if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 70. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. 71. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 72. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 73. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 74. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown.
